summary: Remotely accessed software is a taxable supply of intangible personal property or a service, taxed at the GST or HST rate of the province where the supply is made.

citations.title: CRA, GST/HST and e-commerce
citations.quote: Supplies of intangible personal property (for example, a supply of software or a subscription to a website)

citations.title: CRA, GST/HST and e-commerce
citations.quote: If the supply is made in a participating province, you must charge the HST that applies for that province.

citations.title: GST/HST Technical Information Bulletin B-090, GST/HST and Electronic Commerce (July 2002), Example 6
citations.quote: Consequently, this is characterized as a supply of a service.

notes: Whether hosted software is intangible personal property or a service changes the place-of-supply rule, not the treatment: either way it is taxable for a Canadian resident consumer (no Schedule V or VI provision applies). B-090 (2002, quoting old 7%/15% rates) shows the characterization predates 2013. Exports to non-residents (Schedule VI Part V) are outside the code's scope.

summary: Custom software development is a taxable supply of a service or intangible personal property at the GST or HST rate of the province.

citations.title: CRA, Type of supply (GST/HST)
citations.quote: Most property and services supplied in or imported into Canada are subject to GST/HST (taxable).

citations.title: GST/HST Technical Information Bulletin B-090 (July 2002), Characterization of Supplies
citations.quote: a product is created or developed for a specific customer, but the supplier retains ownership of the product

notes: No CRA publication fetched addresses custom software development directly; 'taxable' rests on the general rule that supplies are taxable unless listed in Schedule V or VI, and no listing covers it. That reasoning is not a direct CRA statement.

summary: Delivery charged by the seller as part of a single supply of the goods follows the goods (e.g. zero-rated for basic groceries); delivery supplied separately is a taxable service.

conditions.when: the seller supplies the goods and delivery together as a single supply and the goods are zero-rated (e.g. basic groceries)
the seller supplies the goods and delivery together as a single supply and the goods are taxable
delivery is supplied separately from the goods (e.g. by a platform or carrier)

citations.title: GST/HST Info Sheet GI-202, Delivery Services Involving Platforms (September 2026)
citations.quote: the GST/HST generally follows the tax treatment of the goods.

citations.title: GST/HST Info Sheet GI-202 (September 2026)
citations.quote: to a consumer as a single supply, the entire supply is zero-rated.

citations.title: GST/HST Policy Statement P-077R2, Single and Multiple Supplies (April 26, 2004)
citations.quote: Equally, separately identified prices for certain elements do not necessarily mean that there are two or more supplies.

citations.title: Canada.ca, GST/HST break - Closed (delivery by an eating establishment)
citations.quote: because it generally has the same tax status as the prepared meal.

notes: The clearest statement (GI-202) is dated September 2026. Before that, the rule rests on P-077R2 (2004, a statement that separately stated prices can still be one supply) and on CRA guidance from 2024-25, so applying it from 2013-04-01 is an inference and unverified as an explicit CRA statement for that period. Whether a seller's separately stated delivery charge is one supply with the goods is a question of fact. Mixed-rate orders: GI-202 says the delivery charge is apportioned among the goods (not quoted here). During Dec 14, 2024 to Feb 15, 2025, seller-billed delivery of relieved goods or meals followed their zero-rating.
